title: Secrets Resilience and Audit Runbook
summary: Practical runbook for handling secret incidents, vault rotations, break-glass access, and packaging audit evidence for SIEM exports. Covers RBAC v2 mappings, audit log schema, automated evidence collection, and post-incident steps.
content:
Purpose and scope:
This runbook is a pragmatic operational guide for Security and SRE when dealing with secrets incidents (exposed credentials, failed rotations, vault compromise, or emergency access). It is designed to: 1) contain and recover credentials, 2) rotate and reissue secrets with minimal blast radius, 3) collect tamper-evident audit evidence for forensics and SIEM ingestion, and 4) align with RBAC v2 policies so actions are traceable.

Quick decision flow (one-liner):
- If credentials are confirmed exposed: trigger containment -> break-glass if needed -> rotate impacted secrets -> deploy compensating config -> collect evidence -> run postmortem.

Primary contacts:
- Incident lead (security): Maya Singh (on-call)
- SRE escalation: Jon Alvarez
- Secrets automation owner: Priya Kapoor
- Legal & privacy: Liam O'Neill
- Pager channel: #sec-incident-response (use thread per incident)

Break-glass access procedure (short):
1) Only available to RBAC v2 role EmergencyAccess (time-limited session). Must be requested in the incident Slack thread and approved by two of: Security Lead, SRE Manager, or Legal.
2) Approval recorded in the incident Slack thread and Jira ticket. Approval must include: reason, scope (systems/paths), duration (max 2 hours), and reviewer names.
3) Security operator runs the break-glass automation which: issues ephemeral credential via Vault/STS, logs session id to audit log, and attaches a signed attestation to evidence bundle.
4) After session ends, automation triggers immediate rotation of any secrets used and generates a verification checklist.

RBAC v2 mapping (high level):
- EmergencyAccess: allowed only for break-glass flows, MFA required, ephemeral tokens, requires 2 approvers. Audit mode: full keystroke/session logging optional depending on sensitivity.
- SecretsAdmin: role that can create policies and manage rotation templates, NO direct access to plaintext secrets unless via ephemeral issuance.
- SecretsReader: read-only metadata access (no ability to view plaintext), used by dashboards.
- ServiceRole_X: limited to reading specific secret paths (path-based policy) and bound to workload identity.
Notes: enforce least privilege, and use path-based deny-lists for highly-sensitive keys (HSM keys, master-encryption-key).

Vaulting and rotation playbook (procedural):
A. Identification phase
- Tag impacted secrets in inventory with incident id (inventory path + hash).
- Flag dependent services (from service-to-secret map).
B. Containment phase
- Revoke any active leases or tokens linked to the secret path.
- Update routing/feature-flagging to disable consumer services if needed.
C. Rotation phase (automated preferred)
- Run rotation pipeline: pull rotation template -> create new secret version -> update secret reference (route traffic) -> increment version and mark old as deprecated -> record rotation metadata in audit store.
- If rotation is manual: perform in maintenance window with two operators and record all steps.
D. Verification and redeploy
- Smoke-test dependent services using canary credentials in staging.
- Promote to production via controlled rollout (canary -> batch -> full).

Audit log schema (core fields):
- event_id: string UUID
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- actor: principal id (user:alice or service:payments-web)
content_continued:
- actor_role: the RBAC v2 role that granted the session
- action: enum{issue,read,rotate,revoke,approve,deny,break_glass_start,break_glass_end}
- secret_path: vault path or service-key id
- request_id: correlated request/trace id for distributed tracing
- outcome: success|failure|partial
- evidence_ref: pointer to evidence bundle (S3 path)
- audit_digest: SHA256 of bundle for tamper-evidence
- origin_ip, agent_string, session_id, duration_ms
Notes: ensure logs are immutable (append-only) and shipped to SIEM within 5 minutes. Include token-less references only (do not store plaintext).

SIEM export mapping (example Splunk/Datadog fields):
- Splunk: index=sec_audit sourcetype=redwood:secrets event_id, timestamp, actor, action, secret_path, outcome, evidence_ref, audit_digest
- Datadog: tags=[role:<actor_role>,action:<action>,outcome:<outcome>], timestamp, event.payload = json(audit fields)
Useful queries:
- "Find all rotate actions in the last 24h with outcome=failure" -> Splunk: index=sec_audit action=rotate outcome=failure | stats count by secret_path
- "List break-glass sessions in the last 90 days" -> Splunk: index=sec_audit action=break_glass_start OR action=break_glass_end | table timestamp actor evidence_ref

Evidence automation and packaging (for forensics):
- Trigger: incident creation in Jira (SEC-913) triggers the evidence collector lambda.
- Collected items: audit logs (last 90 days for involved entities), lease/token revocation artifacts, vault access logs, ephemeral session recordings (if enabled), approval messages (Slack thread export), rotation pipeline logs, and service-level traces for correlated request_id.
- Packaging: collector assembles a gzipped tarball with a manifest.json (manifest is a flat JSON list with file metadata), signs the bundle with KMS key, uploads to S3 (secure-bucket/incident-<id>/evidence-<ts>.tar.gz.sig) and writes a pointer into the audit store.
- Tamper-evidence: include audit_digest in top-level audit log entry. Store signature in separate key-protected store (HSM or KMS).

Retention and legal hold:
- Standard evidence retention: 1 year encrypted; high-sensitivity incidents: legal hold until release by Legal.
- Deletion requires multi-party approval: Security Lead + Legal.

Post-incident checklist (short):
- Confirm rotation complete and no clients use deprecated tokens.
- Run full CI smoke test and monitor error rates for 72 hours.
- Publish incident summary (sanitized) to the exec channel and append to incident Jira.
- Schedule postmortem with owners and create action items with owners and deadlines.

Automation appendices (notes for engineers):
- Rotation pipeline uses: terraform-managed rotation templates, GitOps-driven operator, and vault-plugin for provider-specific rotations. Use feature-flag to toggle automated vs manual mode per secret path.
- Evidence collector: Node lambda that queries the immutable audit-store (S3+Dynamo index), bundles artifacts, and calls KMS.Sign. Must run in VPC if evidence includes VPC-only logs.
- SIEM forwarder: Fluentd daemon on audit-store that converts fields to Splunk json and POSTs to HEC using token-based auth; also emits to Datadog via API key.

Open questions / action items:
- Should break-glass sessions record keystroke-level telemetry for all high-sensitivity paths? (sec-team proposal: opt-in per-incident only)
- Add a cron job to re-verify rotation templates monthly and fail on drift (owner: Priya).
- Improve service-to-secret mapping automation (issue: INFRA-1142).

Appendix: quick commands and examples
- Revoke leases: vault lease revoke -prefix secret/data/production/payments
- Rotate via pipeline: ./scripts/rotate-secret --path secret/data/production/payments --dry-run
- Evidence packer (example): node tools/evidence-packer.js --incident SEC-913 --out s3://secure-bucket/incident-SEC-913/evidence-20260101.tar.gz

Revision history:
- 2025-11-18: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-12-03: added SIEM mapping and packaging flow (Jon)
- 2026-02-15: updated RBAC v2 notes and post-incident checklist (Priya)

Notes to reviewers: this doc is intended as an operational runbook rather than legal artifact. For legal preservation please follow Legal's evidence handling SOP (linked).
